title: Support for Children with Special Needs and Their Caregivers
what_it_is: Support for Children with Special Needs and Their Caregivers

sections.label: Support for special needs students
sections.summary: Questions asked about numbers of students needing extra learning support or with special needs, and support for them, caregivers and ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students are there currently in mainstream schools who have been diagnosed as requiring extra learning support or having special needs; and (b) what additional support has been mandated and available to these students and their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) in the last three years, whether there is an increase in the number of persons with disability, particularly among the student population; and (b) whether the Ministry has plans to improve the support for caregivers of persons with disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will strengthen its support for (i) parents and caregivers of children with special needs and (ii) ageing parents who are caring for their grown-up children with special needs.

sections.label: TRANSIT programme for Primary 1
sections.summary: The TRANSIT programme for Primary 1 students with social and behavioural needs was announced last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last year, we announced that we are rolling out the TRANsition Support for InTegration, or TRANSIT programme, for Primary 1 students with social and behavioural needs.

sections.label: SPED and special educational needs numbers
sections.summary: About 7,000 students, or 20% of those reported with special educational needs, attend 22 SPED schools, with numbers rising about 5% in three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Currently, approximately 7,000 students, or about 20% of all students reported with special educational needs, attend the existing 22 SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Across mainstream and SPED schools, the number of students reported with special educational needs has risen by about 5% in the last three years, largely due to growing awareness and early identification.

sections.label: SPED to post-school transition planning
sections.summary: MOE and partners implement transition planning, School-to-Work Transition Programme and post-school options for SPED students and graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To help students and families transit from SPED to post-school life, MOE works with the SPED schools to implement school-wide processes of transition planning for students at the Secondary years, where each student has an Individual Transition Plan reflecting his or her post-school interests, strengths and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE also works with MSF, SG Enable and the SPED schools for the School-to-Work Transition Programme, to support work-capable students in transiting from school to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For SPED graduates who do not transit to employment due to higher needs, MOE works with SPED schools and SG Enable to facilitate their transition to post-school options based on their abilities and needs, including for students identified for MSF-funded services.

sections.label: SG Enable disability support touchpoint
sections.summary: SG Enable was set up in 2013 and is now the single touchpoint for disability and caregiver support services and public education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: SG Enable was set up in 2013 to support persons with disabilities and is now the single touchpoint for disability and caregiver support services, as well as public education efforts.

sections.label: Parents' guide on developmental needs
sections.summary: The parents' guide will cover developmental needs, access to EI services, transition to school-age provisions, self-care strategies and resources, expected by April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The parents' guide will include information on developmental needs, ways to access EI services, support available to facilitate the child's transition from the preschool years to school-age provisions, as well as self-care strategies and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We expect the guide to be ready by April this year.

sections.label: Parenting Support Providers appointed
sections.summary: MSF appointed 10 Parenting Support Providers offering evidence-based parenting support programmes for parents and caregivers of children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: MSF has also appointed 10 Parenting Support Providers that offer evidence-based parenting support programmes for parents and caregivers of children.

sections.label: Emotional support from caregivers
sections.summary: Family, friends and other caregivers should provide emotional support, and everyone can help by extending a helping hand or listening ear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In addition to having services and programmes available for them and their loved ones, it is equally important for family, friends and other caregivers to provide emotional support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Let us all play a part by extending a helping hand or a listening ear when we see someone in need.

sections.label: Special student care centres
sections.summary: There are eight special student care centres, and early diagnosis gives better touch points on timing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In terms of institutional support, we have, for example, special student care centres, we have eight of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Fortunately, today, since last week, for the longest time that we have been organising, we now have better touch points on the time because we now diagnose the children early, we know who the parents are and, therefore, we can do these touch points earlier.

sections.label: Tracking children in school
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry tracks how these children are doing in school.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, how does the Ministry track how these children are doing in school?

sections.label: Completion and registry suggestion
sections.summary: The work is hoped to be completed within this year or earlier, taking inputs on board including a registry suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We hope that this will be completed within this year, if not, earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And we will take those inputs on board, including the suggestion by the Member, to have a registry.

sections.label: Continuum of care review
sections.summary: MOE and MSF regularly review the master plan for a continuum of care across the life cycle for special needs children and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Because it is so hard, I think we are all even more determined to want to do better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, the first point is, yes, MOE and MSF, we are regularly reviewing the master plan on how we can provide the continuum of care across the entire life cycle stage, for both the special needs children and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I know that for many of the special needs families, the part that is most challenging, the part that is most worrying for all the families with special needs children is: "what happens when we are no longer around?", "what is the care arrangement, what are the financial arrangements that we need to put in place to take care of our children with special needs?" And this is where we will double down our efforts to see how we can provide a more seamless continuum, from the school years to the post-school years in terms of care, work arrangements and also financial independence.
